questions.q: According to the summary, what would fixing sanitation worldwide cost, and what would it save?
a: About $95 billion to fix, saving about $660 billion
About $660 billion to fix, saving about $95 billion
About $1 billion to fix, saving about $100 million
About $100 million to fix, saving about $1 billion
questions.why: Lesson 1 sets the global bill at roughly $95 billion and the eventual saving at $660 billion, since prevention costs less than repair.

questions.q: What did scientist Gary Ruvkun call the biggest factor in living a long, healthy life?
a: Access to a toilet
Access to clean drinking water
A diet rich in vegetables
Regular medical checkups
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites Ruvkun's view that toilet access matters most, and that it could add around 20 years to a person's lifespan.

questions.q: Why does the summary criticize how USAID spends its budget?
a: It funds clean water, which cuts diarrhea less than sanitation would
It ignores the need for clean water entirely
It spends most of its money building latrines
It puts education ahead of basic infrastructure
questions.why: Lesson 2 says USAID spends 90 percent on water, which reduces diarrhea by 20 percent, rather than on sanitation, which would cut it by 40 percent.

questions.q: How did Kamal Kar get villagers to change their sanitation habits?
a: He showed them how much excrement surrounded their village
He paid each family to build its own latrine
He threatened fines for open defecation
He handed out free soap and medicine
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes Kar walking villagers through the area and estimating 120,000 tons of waste, which disgusted them into a cleanup.

questions.q: Which use of human waste does the summary describe?
a: Converting it into biogas for cooking and power
Refining it into a substitute for cement
Filtering it into clean drinking water
Packing it into insulation for homes
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes biogas digesters in rural China that turn waste into power and leave fertilizer behind, boosting vegetable yields.
